title: poc-rollout-lab-hands-on-deployments
content:
Purpose:
This hands-on lab guide is designed for Solutions Engineering workshops with customers who want to validate Redwood inference behavior for: canary model rollouts, multi-variant fallback, and a simple private (VPC/on-prem) deployment footprint. The goal is to run a short PoC during a half-day workshop where attendees can: deploy a small model, exercise routing rules, and observe metrics (latency, token cost, error rate).

Scope and learning objectives:
- Deploy a minimal Private deployment (single-node k8s or small VM) running a sample LLM runtime and register it to the Redwood control plane (local demo mode).
- Create two model variants (v1: float16, v2: int8 quantized) and perform a canary rollout (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%).
- Configure routing policy with fallback to hosted model if private capacity is constrained.
- Validate end-to-end: send requests, inspect traces, and interpret latency/cost tradeoffs.

Audience:
Customer ML engineers, platform engineers, SREs, and product leads. Assumes familiarity with kubectl, Docker, curl, and a basic REST API.

Estimated duration: 3.5 hours (half-day)
- 20m: intro and architecture walkthrough
- 40m: environment setup and private demo deploy
- 1h: model variant creation and canary rollout exercises
- 40m: routing/fallback and lab scenarios
- 10m: wrap-up and next steps

Prerequisites (attendees):
- Laptop with: Docker (local), kubectl, Python 3.10+, curl
- Access to workshop VPC or local k3s cluster (instructions below for kind/k3s)
- Redwood sandbox API key (we provide per-workshop keys)
- GitHub repo cloned: git@github.com:redwood-inference/examples.git (branch: se-workshop)

Workshop environment setup notes (quick):
1) Start a local k3s cluster (recommended for offline workshops):
- curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -s - --no-deploy=traefik
- export KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml
2) Apply a minimal namespace and serviceaccount for the demo:
- kubectl create namespace redwood-demo
- kubectl -n redwood-demo create serviceaccount demo-sa
3) Run a tiny demo runtime container (prebuilt image):
- kubectl -n redwood-demo run demo-runtime --image=ghcr.io/redwood-inference/demo-runtime:stable --port=8080 --env="REDWOOD_MODE=private"
4) Confirm runtime is reachable: kubectl -n redwood-demo port-forward svc/demo-runtime 8080:8080 &
- curl http://localhost:8080/health -> {"status":"ok"}

Registering runtime with control plane (local demo):
- For workshop brevity we use the sandbox control plane token. Example curl to register: 
  curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/runtimes/register \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"name":"demo-node-1","endpoint":"http://10.0.0.5:8080","capabilities":["generation","kv-cache"]}'
- Expected response: {"id":"rt_abc123", "status":"registered"}

Sample model variant packaging (local artifact):
- We ship two lightweight model artifacts for the lab: small-gpt-fp16.tgz and small-gpt-int8.tgz (quantized). Uploads simulated in the sandbox: 
  curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/upload \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" \n    -F "file=@small-gpt-fp16.tgz" \n    -F "name=small-gpt" \n    -F "variant=fp16"
- Repeat for variant=int8.
- The control plane will return model IDs like mdl_01_fp16 and mdl_01_int8.

Creating a canary rollout (control plane API example):
- Create initial deployment pointing at fp16 variant (100%):
  curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/deployments \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"name":"customer-demo","routes":[{"model_id":"mdl_01_fp16","weight":100}],"runtimes":["rt_abc123"]}'
- Confirm traffic route: GET /deployments/customer-demo -> shows one route.
- Canary: gradually add int8 variant and shift weights:
  PATCH /deployments/customer-demo with body: '{"routes":[{"model_id":"mdl_01_fp16","weight":90},{"model_id":"mdl_01_int8","weight":10}]}'
- After observation (latency and quality checks) move to 50/50 then 100% int8.

Example Python snippet to call deployment and measure latency: 
- python code (workshop file: examples/workshop/call_and_measure.py)

import time
import requests

API_URL = "https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/generate"
API_KEY = "${WORKSHOP_TOKEN}"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
def call(prompt):
    payload = {"deployment":"customer-demo","input":prompt}
    t0 = time.time()
    r = requests.post(API_URL, headers=HEADERS, json=payload, timeout=15)
    dt = time.time() - t0
    return r.json(), dt

if __name__ == '__main__':
    for p in ["Summarize this paragraph.", "Generate a short poem about lakes."]:
        resp, latency = call(p)
        print(p, "->", latency, "s", resp.get('output', '')[:120])

(Attendees will run this locally and record per-variant latencies.)

Kubernetes rollout example (for private runtime with native pod variants):
- We also demo a k8s-native canary where two Deployments run different model runners (fp16 vs int8) and a Service selects via an Istio traffic-split for weights. Minimal YAML snippet below (expanded files in repo):

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-runner-fp16
  namespace: redwood-demo
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-runner
      variant: fp16
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: model-runner
        variant: fp16
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: runner
        image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runner:fp16
        env:
        - name: MODEL_PATH
          value: "/models/small-gpt-fp16"

---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: model-svc
  namespace: redwood-demo
spec:
  hosts: ["model-svc.internal"]
  http:
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: model-runner
        subset: fp16
      weight: 90
    - destination:
        host: model-runner
        subset: int8
      weight: 10

(This is intentionally simplified — repo includes complete manifests and kustomize overlays.)

Routing policy with fallback to hosted variants:
- Workshop exercise: configure the deployment so that if private runtime latency > 1.5s or error rate > 2% for 2 consecutive minutes, the control plane automatically routes to the Redwood hosted model for that route.
- Example policy (pseudo-JSON for the control plane):
  {
    "deployment":"customer-demo",
    "fallback":{
      "trigger": {"latency_ms": 1500, "error_rate_pct": 2, "window_seconds": 120},
      "fallback_target": "hosted-small-gpt"
    }
  }
- During the lab, participants will simulate runtime degradation by introducing CPU throttling (kubectl exec into pod and run a stress loop) and verify the fallback is triggered and traffic shifts.

Validation checklist (what to observe):
- Canary metrics: per-variant 95th percentile latency, token-usage cost, and output quality delta using a short eval set (we provide a 20-prompt set).
- Rollback: trigger an automatic rollback when quality regression > 6% (we'll show how to set an eval-based alert).
- Fallback: confirm hosted route receives traffic and request latency remains within SLA.
- Tracing: use the Redwood Console (demo) to view a trace for one request and identify where KV cache hits/misses occurred.

Troubleshooting notes (common issues in workshops):
- Registration failed: check token and network ACLs. Use curl -v to see 403 vs 401.
- Upload errors: large tarballs may time out; recommend pre-pulled artifacts in the cluster image registry for the workshop to reduce delays.
- Istio not splitting traffic: ensure DestinationRule subsets are defined and labels match exactly.
- Simulated degradation doesn't trigger fallback: check evaluation windows and metric ingestion delay (Prometheus scrape interval).

Exercises and tasks for attendees (grouped):
A) Quick win (20m):
- Register runtime, upload fp16 model, create deployment, call endpoint, capture latency.
B) Canary flow (40m):
- Add int8 variant, shift 10% traffic, run eval set and compare outputs, shift to 50/50, then 100% if quality acceptable.
C) Failure and fallback (40m):
- Inject load to private runtime, confirm fallback to hosted occurs, and measure end-to-end latency.
D) Observability (20m):
- Create a per-route dashboard showing token-cost, p95 latency, error rate, and model variant composition. Spot anomalies.

Deliverables for the customer post-workshop (we provide):
- A short PoC report with: configuration snippets used, results (latency, cost delta, quality diff), and recommended next steps for Dedicated sizing or Private rollout.
- GitHub repo branch with all workshop manifests and scripts.
- Optional template for an enterprise-grade Canary Runbook (inc: alerts, thresholds, and contact list).

Next steps and variations to suggest to customers:
- If the customer prefers no control-plane registration in their environment, show the on-prem-only recipe that uses a lightweight control proxy and out-of-band metrics export.
- For heavy throughput workloads, iterate on batching and KV cache settings (we include a short lab that toggles batch size and measures tokens/sec).
- Enterprise follow-up: schedule a 2-day on-site PoC to validate Dedicated capacity sizing and cost modeling.

Notes to SE running this lab:
- Pre-create the two model artifacts in the sandbox and share URLs; avoid workshop time spent on long uploads.
- Have a Plan B: if attendees have limited permissions, run the k8s exercises in a shared namespace and give read-only access to participants to avoid permission issues.
- Bring a small handout (one pager) that lists the commands used in the lab and typical trouble commands (kubectl logs, kubectl exec, curl -v).

Appendix: quick commands cheat-sheet
- Check runtime health: curl http://localhost:8080/health
- Register runtime: curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/runtimes/register -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" -d '{"name":"demo-node-1","endpoint":"http://10.0.0.5:8080"}'
- Upload model: curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" -F "file=@small-gpt-int8.tgz" -F "variant=int8"
- Create deployment: curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/deployments -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" -d '{"name":"customer-demo","routes":[{"model_id":"mdl_01_fp16","weight":100}]}'
- Canary patch: curl -X PATCH https://sandbox.redwood.ai/api/v1/deployments/customer-demo -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_TOKEN" -d '{"routes":[{"model_id":"mdl_01_fp16","weight":90},{"model_id":"mdl_01_int8","weight":10}]}'

End of doc.
